question: What is a feature of EPLD upgrades on a Cisco Nexus 7000 Series Switch?
options: They do not cause service disruptions.
They are performed during an ISSU system and kickstart upgrade.
They are independent of the Cisco NX-OS ISSU process.
They execute simultaneously on multiple modules.
theory: EPLD (erasable programmable logic device, e.g., FPGA) images control lower-level hardware functions on Nexus 7000 line cards and are versioned and applied completely separately from the NX-OS system/kickstart images used in an ISSU. EPLD upgrades are always disruptive since they reload the affected module, are applied one module at a time rather than simultaneously, and Cisco explicitly recommends against performing them during or around an ISSU — which is why their defining characteristic is being independent of the ISSU process, not being nondisruptive or simultaneous. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — EPLD Upgrades)
